newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ISSUE DEPT ASSETS UP TO 3.08 BLN MARKS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ISSUE DEPT ASSETS UP TO 3.08 BLN MARKS.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank's Issue Department assets and liabilities inched up to 3.080 billion marks on July 11 from 3.002 billion marks a week earlier, the BNB said on Monday.

The cash in nostro and vostro accounts in foreign currencies of the assets has risen to the equivalent of 1.444 trillion levs by some 574 billion levs from 869.7 billion a week ago, while the Banking Department deposit of the liabilities has declined to 528 billion levs from 535 billion levs.
BNB officials were not immidately available for comment.

The department's assets include the mark equivalent of 990 billion levs in securities, 1.444 trillion levs cash and nostro accounts in foreign currencies, 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and 5.3 billion levs in accrued intrest receivable, said the BNB in a statement.

The department's liabilities comprise 714.5 billion levs of currency in circulation, 772.4 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts, 481.8 billion levs in government deposits and accounts, 572.3 billion levs in a State Fund for Reconstruction and Development account, 8.0 billion levs in other deposits and accrued interest payable of 3.1 billion levs.

These liabilities also include a 528 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department that can be used for lending to sound banks, only when the functioning of the banking and payments system is threatened.
The primary objective of the Banking Department is to ensure confidence in the liquidity of the the banking system and more broadly the efficient functioning of key financial markets.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund Bulgaria introduced on July 1 the currency board, a fixed exchange rate mechanism which requires levs in circulation to be matched by BNB foreign exchange reserves.
Under the arrangement the lev is pegged to the mark as anchor currency at 1,000 levs. The system bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
The balance sheet is published weekly. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
